messages:
sam (customer): hey team — getting a bunch of 429s right now on our prod key even though the org quota in the console shows ~60% remaining. started after a deploy ~10:15 UTC. any idea?

emily (support): sorry you're seeing this, can you paste a sample request id / key id and approximate timestamps? 429 body and any X-RateLimit headers would help. also are you using any proxy that might collapse many clients to one IP?

sam (customer): request id in logs: req_0a7f3c. 429 response: `{
  "error": "rate_limit_exceeded",
  "retry_after": 1
}` but no X-RateLimit-* headers. we do have a legacy NAT gateway in front of the app — but only a handful of pods. traffic spiked from 200 -> 2k rps for ~30s after the deploy.

emily (support): thanks. two quick clarifications: (1) which api key (last 6 chars ok) and is it tied to a project or org-level key? (2) can you grep for LF logs that show `quota_scope` or `limit_scope` in the request tracing? that will tell us whether requests were hitting org or project scope.

sam (customer): key ends …a7c9. looks like a project key (created ages ago). console shows project quota 100k/min, org quota 500k/min. we were under project quota but getting 429s.

emily (support): hmmm. that suggests either: (A) IP-based burst limits triggered, or (B) the key is being misattributed to a different scope at the routing layer. i'm going to pull logs from the rate limiter. tagging jae. @jae can you check rate-limiter logs for key …a7c9 around 1798428800-1798429000?

jae (support-engineer): on it. attaching quick grep:```
# grep for key a7c9
2026-03-11T10:14:55Z req=req_0a7f3c key_suffix=a7c9 client_ip=34.203.11.12 scope=project project_id=proj-42 org_id=org-77 limit_bucket=project:proj-42:gen_text burst_count=220
2026-03-11T10:14:56Z req=req_0a7f3d key_suffix=a7c9 client_ip=34.203.11.12 scope=project project_id=proj-42 org_id=org-77 limit_bucket=ip:34.203.11.12:gen_text burst_count=220
2026-03-11T10:15:10Z req=req_0a7f4a key_suffix=a7c9 client_ip=34.203.11.12 scope=project project_id=proj-42 org_id=org-77 limit_bucket=ip:34.203.11.12:gen_text burst_count=900
```

emily (support): interesting — limiter shows two different limit_bucket entries: project:proj-42:gen_text and ip:34.203.11.12:gen_text. the second line suggests IP-based bucket is being consumed heavily. do you have many clients NATed behind that same public IP?

sam (customer): yes, our k8s cluster egress is a single NAT IP (we use a small cluster). thought per-key limits would be the limiter, not per-IP. is this expected?

emily (support): by design our rate limiter enforces multiple dimensions: per-key (project), per-org, and per-egress-IP. IP buckets are a safety for excessive bursts that could originate from many distinct consumer tokens collapsed by NAT/proxy. default IP bucket is fairly conservative. this explains why project quota looked fine but you still hit 429s.

sam (customer): ok that makes sense — any short-term mitigations? we can't change infra quickly.

emily (support): short-term options: (1) create a second API key and distribute traffic across keys (this spreads across per-key buckets), (2) request a temporary IP-burst exemption from us while you migrate to multiple egress IPs, or (3) reduce burst by rate-limiting at your side (client side smoothing). i can open a temporary quota bump for the IP-burst bucket — will need approval from infra. want me to start that?

sam (customer): yes please open a temporary allowance for the next 2 hours while we roll a new egress. also we'd like the root cause so we can avoid.

emily (support): starting escalation. @rate-limiter-bot, open incident for IP-burst-exception for ip=34.203.11.12 duration=2h reason="customer NATed cluster causing IP limit"

rate-limiter-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-2219. Assigned to infra-rate-limiter. Priority: P2. TTL 2h.

jae (support-engineer): pinging infra ops. quick note on an edge case we sometimes see: if a key was created before a migration where keys were split from org->project, the key metadata can have stale scope markers. that can cause the gateway to attach both project and org attributes to requests and sometimes the IP fallback logic treats those as separate buckets. asking infra to check for dual-scoped keys for proj-42.

infra-note (from ops): checked INC-2026-2219 — key …a7c9 was minted before the org->project split and had an empty project tag in our legacy index; at the gateway a recent fix added heuristics that set both project_id and org_id when project tag missing, which in combination with NATed IP created an unexpected hot IP bucket. we applied a temporary IP-burst override for 2h and also backfilled key metadata to mark the key as project-scoped only.

sam (customer): confirmed traffic normalized after ~3m post-override, 429s stopped. thanks. what are permanent fixes?

emily (support): recommendations: (1) update your egress to multiple IPs or use Cloud NAT with a range, (2) rotate to multiple API keys for high-volume clients, (3) we will harden gateway heuristics so pre-migration keys no longer create mixed-scope buckets, (4) you can also request per-key burst tuning on Dedicated plans. i'll follow up with a RFC on the gateway change.

sam (customer): appreciated. one more ask — can you add X-RateLimit headers to the 429s? that would make it easier to debug next time.

jae (support-engineer): agree. filing FEAT-987 to add X-RateLimit-{limit,remaining,reset,scope} headers for all limiter responses. tagging devex and console for visibility.

emily (support): closing this thread since INC-2026-2219 has the temporary mitigation and infra is tracking the gateway fix. please reopen if you see any recurrence. :thumbsup:
